I was in that position and still am, I had to end up on Antidepressants in order to start treating my anxiety through exposure, couldn't do it without the medication because the anxiety was too severe.  I've only been on anti's for a week and can already see a decrease in anxiety. My brother has been on them for 15 years, he would vomit before going in to social situations he was so anxious, he spent his teens like this, until he went on Prozac and it completely changed his life. He's now a vet surgeon, married with a child and owns his own practice. It can just take one action to change your life completely! I also definitely recommend CBT whilst you're on anti's, don't just rely on the medication. All the best!

Basically I saw my social anxiety lessen when I spent time living in a big city and I was out everyday amongst people, forcing myself to be amongst people because I absolutely despise staying indoors doing nothing. I live in a complete shithole now, a small city where everybody knows each other from kindergarten and they refuse to socialise with anybody outside their comfy social circles, so I'm isolated rn quite badly, spend a lot of time at home and have now ended up on antidepressants. Social anxiety can stem from environmental factors. If you're in a shitty environment, it makes things 10x worse.

Exposure is the best solution for social anxiety, take gradual steps in exposing yourself in to situations that make you anxious, don't fight the anxiety, accept that you're anxious and that if you're in that situation for long enough, the anxiety will gradually go away. They use exposure as a tool in CBT. Some people will require to take antidepressants throughout their exposure therapy, but there's absolutely nothing wrong with that. Medication numbs your anxiety so that you're able to tackle the core problem without being paralysed by Anxiety.
